newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia probes Surgutneftegaz share issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia probes Surgutneftegaz share issue.

text.p: Russia's main securities watchdog said on Monday it was examining oil company AO Surgutneftegaz's supplementary share issue after numerous inquiries from investors and urged the Finance Ministry to suspend the issue.
The Federal Commission for the Securities Market said in a statement it was checking whether investors' rights had been violated in the issue.
It said it had made a proposal to the Finance Ministry on Sunday to suspend the issue and not to register it until the checks were completed.
The commission said that when the checks were made it would present its conclusions to the ministry on whether the issue should be allowed to stand or be declared invalid.

The oil company's parent Surgut Holding (NK Surgutneftegaz) said late last month it had acquired an entire new issue of 500 million ordinary shares and 34.02 million preferred shares in Surgutneftegaz, raising its stake to 43.5 percent from 38 percent.
A senior official of Surgut Holding said the shares would not reach the secondary market but some analysts said the issue was still a dilution of other shareholders' stakes.
Surgut Holding said the issue was made in accordance with the company's charter, approved by shareholders in June, and was intended to strengthen control over the subsidiary.
Investment bank Renaissance Capital said the shares were bought for a combined $0.18 each, far below the market price.
Surgutneftegaz shares stood at $0.415 on the Russian Trading System at 1010 GMT after closing on Sunday, a trading day after two market holidays last week, at $0.408.
A Surgut Holding spokesman said the company was aware of the inquiry and was waiting for further information from the commission.
